Description:
L’objet de cet article est d’étudier une nouvelle approche de détection fiable de changements brusques (ruptures) dans un systeme stochastique. Il y a un certain nombre d’applications ou le probleme de sécurité est primordial. Dans ce type d’application, l’utilisateur exige une détection fiable de ruptures, autrement dit: une détection pendant une durée donnée avec une faible probabilité de non détection pour une probabilité de fausse alarme fixée a priori. Nous envisageons comme application, le contrôle d’intégrité du systeme de positionnement et de navigation par satellites GPS.
Abstract–The goal of this paper is to give a new approach to the reliable detection of abrupt changes in stochastic systems. There are applications where the problem of security is extremely important. The users impose a constraint on the maximum delay for the detection in such a case. Specifically, they fix the probability of missed detection within a given time-to-alarm and the probability of false alarms. The application of the proposed algorithms to the problem of the GPS integrity monitoring is also discussed in the paper.

Authors: Kassem Ahmad, Bassem Bakhache, Safwan El Assad
Description: Satellites are expected to play an important role in providing Internet Protocol (IP) multicast services to complement next-generation terrestrial networks. IP multicast is supported in the next generation of satellite systems implementing DVB-S (Digital Video Broadcasting via Satellite). In this type of communication, security and scalability are the main challenges. Eavesdropping can be easily performed, moreover the large groups size and their members high dynamicity have a significant impact on the network resources due to the high rekeying load. In this paper, a new security system is proposed for IP multicast transmission over DVB-S. This system provides security services required to counteract major attacks on multicast communication. It is based on a new encapsulation method called EULE (Enhanced Unidirectional Lightweight Encapsulation), which works with the label-switching approach to ensure an efficient filtering and multicast forwarding. The proposed system encompasses a new key management scheme which aim to reduce the rekeying cost due to the dynamic nature of multicast groups. This scheme consists of an architecture formed by Two layers of Logical Key Hierarchy (TLKH), based on two independent LKH key distribution layered architecture: a satellite-layer and a terrestrial-layer. The usage of chaos is proposed for the generation of new keys in the two layers and for the encryption of the data and the transmitted keys. For keys transmission, a new type of packet is introduced to transport a set of encrypted keys. This significantly minimizes the number of rekeying messages performed by LKH by a factor of 72%. Description: Steganography is an approach for hiding secret information into a cover (text, audio signal, image,...) in an imperceptibility way. In general, the steganographic algorithm introducing statistical differences between cover and stego works (what the cover becomes after hiding information). In this paper, we aim to analyze these differences for a chaos based steganographic method called EAE-LSB (Enhanced Adaptive data hiding in Edge areas of images with spatial Least Significant Bit domain). We use in this work, a blind steganalysis based on classifying higher-order statistical features for images in the wavelet domain. The goal of steganalysis is to detect and/or estimate potentially hidden information from observed data with little or no knowledge about the steganography algorithm and/or its parameters.
